stories.headline: Mastercard & Sunrate Define 'Agentic Global Payments' at World AI Conference — Maps 13 B2B Agent Use Cases
stories.summary: Mastercard and Sunrate unveiled a joint white paper at the July 23 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, framing B2B cross-border payments as entering a new 'Autonomy' stage — where AI agents independently orchestrate end-to-end payment and treasury workflows under governance controls. The report maps 16 pain points across the B2B payment lifecycle and outlines 13 high-value agent use cases spanning supplier onboarding, FX management, compliance screening, and fraud detection. This is a direct signal that major payment networks are hardening the demand for trusted entity resolution and counterparty data inside agentic workflows — exactly the role D&B's DUNS and Commercial Graph are positioned to fill.

stories.headline: D&B Turns 185 — Reframes Its History as 'Powering the AI Economy'
stories.summary: On July 1, Dun & Bradstreet published a formal 185th anniversary narrative drawing a direct line from its 1841 origins in commercial credit reporting — with Lincoln and Grant among early credit reporters — to its current role as a data layer for agentic AI workflows. The move is a deliberate positioning play: anchoring D&B's modern AI product story in 185 years of proprietary entity and credit data that no challenger can replicate overnight. For the sales and marketing analytics team, this is a ready-made proof point for the 'structural moat' narrative — incumbency and data depth as a competitive advantage AI-native rivals cannot shortcut.

stories.headline: D&B Launches Agentic Compliance Capabilities — AI Agents Now Act Inside Onboarding and Due Diligence Workflows
stories.summary: In mid-June, Dun & Bradstreet announced new agentic capabilities that let AI agents operate directly inside compliance workflows, automating onboarding, screening, and due diligence by combining verified business context with agent execution. This extends D&B's agentic footprint beyond finance and prospecting into the compliance and risk workflow — a high-value, regulation-driven use case where data provenance and entity accuracy are non-negotiable. It validates the 'be everywhere' platform strategy: D&B is now embedding across at least three distinct agent archetypes (Prospecting, Pipeline Risk, and now Compliance/Onboarding).

stories.headline: Apollo.io Plugs Its GTM Data Directly into Perplexity — Signals the 'Data Connector' Race Is Accelerating
stories.summary: On June 3, Apollo.io announced a connector enabling sales teams to access its contact intelligence, intent signals, and workflow capabilities directly inside Perplexity's AI environment — one of several rapid integrations Apollo has shipped as it repositions itself as an 'agentic GTM platform.' The move mirrors the broader pattern of B2B data vendors racing to embed in AI interfaces before platform lock-in solidifies, and underscores that the connector layer — not just the data itself — is becoming a key competitive battleground. For D&B, this reinforces the urgency of the 'be everywhere' distribution strategy: proprietary data stranded outside the agent interfaces buyers are adopting will rapidly lose relevance.

stories.headline: Gartner Warns Agentic AI Entering 'Trough of Disillusionment' — 40% of Enterprise Projects Failing ROI Targets
stories.summary: Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle places AI agents at the peak of inflated expectations and forecasts a trough of disillusionment throughout the year, with analysts noting that most projects remain early-stage experiments that underestimate the real cost and complexity of production deployment. Separately, IDC flags that in Asia-Pacific, 45% of AI use cases are expected to miss ROI targets due to unclear gains and poor data foundations. This is a double-edged signal for D&B: it validates the 'Explainability First / Ground Truth' argument — agents built on poor or unverified data fail — but also means sales conversations need to lead with concrete ROI evidence, not just agentic capability.

stories.headline: OpenAI Ships GPT-5.6 Family — Three-Tier 'Sol, Luna, Terra' Line Goes Live After White House Voluntary Review
stories.summary: OpenAI released its GPT-5.6 line — flagships Sol, Luna, and Terra — to the public on July 9, after a roughly 12-day voluntary security review under the White House's AI executive order framework. The flagship Sol model claims 54% greater token-efficiency on coding tasks than prior versions, with all three tiers aimed explicitly at agentic, multi-step workflows. The release is part of a broader four-lab sprint in July that is rapidly narrowing capability gaps between frontier models and compressing pricing across the board.

stories.headline: Meta Launches 'Meta Compute' — Pivots from AI Buyer to Cloud Seller, Wiping $200B from Chip Stocks
stories.summary: On July 1, Meta announced plans to commercialize its internal AI infrastructure as 'Meta Compute,' offering enterprises both hosted Llama model access via API and raw GPU compute capacity — positioning it directly against AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and neoclouds like CoreWeave. The announcement triggered a sell-off that erased roughly $200 billion in market value from the semiconductor complex, with Micron falling over 10% and AMD nearly 7%, as investors reassessed the 'perpetual AI scarcity' narrative. The move signals that the first wave of hyperscaler AI overbuilding has produced genuine surplus capacity, with structural implications for compute pricing and infrastructure valuations.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K3 — China's Largest Model at 2.8 Trillion Parameters Enters the Frontier Race
stories.summary: Beijing-based Moonshot AI published Kimi K3, its largest model to date at 2.8 trillion parameters, as part of the densely packed July frontier release cycle. In head-to-head agentic coding tests, Kimi K3 ran 2.3x cheaper than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 on the same task, though it consumed more tokens and took longer to complete. The release reinforces that Chinese labs are closing the frontier gap on cost-performance, presenting a direct pricing challenge to Western models and adding a new option for enterprises evaluating agentic AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: U.S. States Have Now Enacted 109 AI Laws in 2026 — California's AI Transparency Act Activates August 2
stories.summary: As of July 1, U.S. states have collectively enacted 109 AI laws and 28 data center laws in 2026, according to the NYU Center on Technology Policy — slightly behind last year's pace but still a historic legislative wave. California's AI Transparency Act becomes operative on August 2, the same day as the EU AI Act's full applicability deadline, creating a simultaneous compliance crunch on both sides of the Atlantic. The federal preemption language in the Senate-passed Great American AI Act adds further uncertainty: if the House concurs, state-level compliance frameworks built over the past 18 months may need to be fundamentally rebuilt.

stories.headline: Burnham Names Full Cabinet in First Week as PM — NHS and Cost of Living Take Centre Stage
stories.summary: Andy Burnham, who took office on 20 July as the UK's seventh prime minister in a decade, spent his first week announcing Cabinet appointments and laying out early priorities. His opening pledge was to end rough sleeping, with a 10-year plan promised later in 2026, while he vowed cost-of-living measures would not 'take risks with the economy'. On foreign policy, Burnham confirmed unwavering support for Ukraine and said President Zelenskyy would be among the first world leaders he called.

stories.headline: U.S. Pauses Iran Bombing Campaign as Netanyahu Flies to Washington
stories.summary: The United States paused a two-week bombing campaign against Iran as of 27 July, with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boarding a plane to Washington for a meeting with President Trump at the White House, where the Iran conflict will top the agenda. Earlier Iranian drone and missile strikes killed three American soldiers at an air base in Jordan. Netanyahu also plans to attend the funeral of the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham while in Washington.

stories.headline: Webb Telescope Finds Giant Hidden Planet in One of Astronomy's Most Famous Systems
stories.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has discovered a giant planet that had been concealed inside one of the most studied star systems in astronomy. The find, announced on 23 July, adds a major new body to a system that scientists thought they understood well. It further demonstrates Webb's ability to reveal objects invisible to earlier observatories.

stories.headline: 21-Year-Old Jackson Koivun Wins 3M Open in Just His Third Pro Start, Beats World No. 1 Scheffler
stories.summary: Jackson Koivun, aged just 21, claimed his first PGA Tour title at TPC Twin Cities on 26 July, firing a closing 5-under 66 to finish at a tournament-record 25-under 259 — three shots clear of world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler. Koivun had entered the final round with a three-shot cushion after shooting 61 in round three, and held his nerve despite hearing the crowd warn 'Scottie's coming' as Scheffler posted a 63. It was only Koivun's third start as a professional, and Scheffler's fifth runner-up finish of the season.

stories.headline: Newcastle's Anthony Gordon Completes £69m Move to Barcelona as Premier League Transfer Window Heats Up
stories.summary: Newcastle United have sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3 million, one of the headline deals of the 2026 Premier League summer transfer window. The window, which runs until 1 September, has already seen significant activity across clubs ahead of the new season kicking off on 22 August. Arsenal enter as defending champions, while Liverpool begin life under new manager Andoni Iraola following a disappointing 2025-26 campaign.

stories.headline: Commonwealth Games Open in Glasgow — Rugby Sevens and New Events Draw Early Crowds
stories.summary: The 2026 Commonwealth Games got under way in Glasgow on 23 July, bringing together athletes from across the Commonwealth in a multi-sport event that includes rugby sevens as one of its marquee competitions. The Games represent a major moment for Scottish sport and are drawing attention ahead of the rugby union calendar's resumption in the autumn. Organisers are hoping Glasgow's hosting will echo the success of the city's acclaimed 2014 edition.

stories.headline: CERN Physicists Take New Look at Why Matter Beat Antimatter After the Big Bang
stories.summary: Physicists at CERN have published fresh results re-examining one of science's biggest open questions: why the universe is made of matter rather than antimatter. The 20 July study takes a new experimental approach to probing CP violation — the subtle asymmetry between matter and antimatter that allowed the universe as we know it to form. The findings add to an accelerating run of particle physics results from CERN in 2026.

stories.headline: Supersizing M&A for the AI Era: Fewer, Bigger Deals as AI Rewrites the Dealmaking Playbook
stories.summary: PwC's Global M&A 2026 Mid-Year Outlook, published early July 2026, argues that AI is driving a structural shift toward fewer but much larger deals, with capital increasingly moving through minority investments, joint ventures, and partnerships rather than outright acquisitions. A landmark signal: Anthropic, Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs announced a joint enterprise AI services company in May 2026 to deploy Claude into core operations — a model PwC sees as indicative of how value creation in AI differs from prior tech waves. For D&B, this validates the 'neutral data layer' thesis: as large platforms consolidate AI capabilities through M&A and partnerships, the proprietary data assets underpinning agent decisions — DUNS, Paydex, corporate family trees — become the scarce, non-replicable inputs that any acquirer or JV must still source externally. D&B's moat compounds precisely because no single M&A transaction can replicate 600M+ records of ground-truth business identity.
stories.source: PwC Global Deals Practice, PwC Global M&A Industry Trends: 2026 Mid-Year Outlook

stories.headline: Agentic AI M&A Has Shifted from Selective to Structural: Enterprise Platforms Are Buying Across the Entire Stack
stories.summary: New Market Pitch's Agentic AI M&A Tracker, widely circulated in late June/early July 2026, documents a near-4x acceleration in agentic AI deal volume — 35 deals in the most recent 12 months versus 9 in the prior year — with buyers now acquiring across customer-service agents, coding agents, IT operations, procurement, compliance, agent security, and data governance layers. The analysis notes that enterprise software platforms are acquiring agents defensively because a third-party agent could become the control layer sitting above Salesforce, ServiceNow, or Zendesk. This is a direct strategic signal for D&B: as platforms race to own the agent orchestration layer, the 'be everywhere' embedding strategy becomes even more critical — D&B's entity resolution and proprietary scores must be wired into every emerging agent framework before platform lock-in hardens. The governance and data quality layer is the last mile that M&A alone cannot easily replicate.
stories.source: New Market Pitch, Agentic AI M&A Tracker (New Market Pitch)

stories.headline: AI-Driven Enterprise Software Spending to Surpass $450B in 2026 — But the Governance Gap Is the Real Story
stories.summary: Intrepid Investment Bankers' M&A Market Monthly for July 2026, combined with corroborating data from the Agentic AI Institute, surfaces a defining tension: AI software spend is projected to grow ~60% year-over-year in 2026, yet 60% of enterprises deploying agents lack formal governance frameworks, and Gartner estimates more than 40% of agentic AI projects launched today will be cancelled by end of 2027 due to cost overruns, unclear business value, or weak risk controls. The deployment boom is running well ahead of the trust and accountability infrastructure needed to sustain it. For D&B, this is the core commercial opportunity: explainability, entity-level ground truth, and structured data provenance are precisely the governance primitives that close the gap between agent deployment and agent accountability — positioning D&B's 'Explainability First' strategy not as a nice-to-have but as a prerequisite for enterprise AI programmes that need to survive board and regulatory scrutiny.
stories.source: Intrepid Investment Bankers, M&A Market Monthly July 2026; corroborating data: Agentic AI Institute / Gartner

data_science.tagline: The shared memory layer that stops your ML teams from recomputing the same features twelve different ways.
data_science.what_it_is: A feature store is a centralised data system that sits between your raw data pipelines and your ML models. It has two jobs: (1) compute and store feature values consistently so every model — whether in training or live inference — sees the same numbers, and (2) serve those features at low latency when an agent or model needs a prediction right now. Think of it as a versioned, queryable library of 'facts about entities' — customers, companies, products — that any model can borrow without rebuilding from scratch. In D&B's world, an entity is almost always a business identified by a DUNS number, making feature stores a natural complement to entity resolution.
data_science.how_it_works:
A feature store has four moving parts:

1. **Feature Pipeline (Offline):** Batch jobs (Spark, dbt, Flink) read raw data and compute features — e.g. 'rolling 90-day Paydex trend for DUNS 123456789'. Results land in an offline store (a data warehouse or Delta Lake table) used for model training.

2. **Online Store:** A low-latency key-value database (Redis, DynamoDB, Bigtable) holds the *latest* feature values per entity. At inference time, a model requests features by entity key and gets a response in <10ms.

3. **Feature Registry:** A catalogue that stores feature definitions, owners, data lineage, and versions. This is what prevents two teams computing 'days_since_last_payment' differently.

4. **Point-in-Time Correctness:** When generating a training dataset, the feature store reconstructs what feature values *looked like at the moment a label was created* — not their current values. This eliminates a subtle but devastating bug called training-serving skew, where a model trains on future-leaked data and fails in production.

Popular open-source options: Feast. Managed options: Tecton, Hopsworks, Databricks Feature Store, Vertex AI Feature Store.
data_science.when_to_use:
Use a feature store when:
- **Multiple models share features:** If your propensity-to-buy model and your churn model both need 'company headcount growth rate', compute it once.
- **Online + offline parity matters:** Any real-time scoring scenario (a sales agent asking 'is this account ready to buy right now?') where training-serving skew would silently corrupt predictions.
- **Feature reuse across teams:** When a data science team in APAC shouldn't have to reverse-engineer what the Americas team built.
- **Regulated or explainable AI contexts:** The registry gives you an audit trail — what feature definition was model v2.3 trained on, and has it drifted?

Do NOT over-engineer with a feature store if you have one model, one team, and purely batch predictions. The overhead isn't worth it at that scale.
data_science.worked_example:
**D&B Account Expansion Agent — 'Buydex Signal Readiness' Scoring**

Scenario: D&B's Account Expansion agent archetype needs to rank existing customers by their likelihood to expand into a new product (e.g. upgrading from basic firmographics to the full Buydex intent signal suite). The agent runs in Salesforce Agentforce and must return a ranked list in real time when a rep opens an account page.

**Without a feature store:** Three separate data science squads each compute their own version of 'Paydex momentum', 'corporate family tree expansion rate', and 'recent employee growth'. Each squad's definition drifts. The training dataset leaks future Paydex values. The live Salesforce call hits a slow SQL query and times out.

**With a feature store (Tecton + Redis):**
- An offline Spark pipeline runs nightly, computing ~40 DUNS-level features: rolling Paydex z-score (30/60/90d), corporate family tree new subsidiary additions (L12M), firmographic volatility index, prior product adoption breadth, days since last CRM interaction.
- These land in the offline store for model retraining and in Redis for live serving.
- Point-in-time correctness ensures the training labels (expansion event date) align to feature snapshots *before* the expansion — no leakage.
- The Feature Registry records that 'paydex_zscore_90d_v2' replaced 'paydex_zscore_90d_v1' on 2026-03-15, with the change documented.
- When the Agentforce expansion agent fires, it calls the feature store with a DUNS key, gets 40 features back in 8ms, scores the model, and returns a ranked recommendation with SHAP-based plain-English rationale ('This account's Paydex score improved 1.8 standard deviations over 90 days while adding 3 subsidiaries — high readiness signal.').
- **Result:** Model retraining time drops 60% (no feature recompute), three teams share the same definitions, and the live agent response is well within Salesforce's UI latency budget.
resources: Feast open-source feature store documentation and quickstart guide (feast.dev) — best starting point for hands-on implementation
'Rethinking Feature Stores' — Tecton engineering blog series covering point-in-time correctness, online/offline architecture, and real-world MLOps patterns
'Designing Machine Learning Systems' by Chip Huyen (O'Reilly, 2022) — Chapter 7 covers feature engineering and feature stores with production-grade depth
